guide: Open Start and type your imprint name, your cash floor, the months of cover you want, the owner draw you plan, the set-aside percent (confirm it with your tax adviser) and the date and amount of your next tax payment.
Check Team and Stores. Team holds the phones for the message links; Stores holds the payment delay of each store, which the receipts forecast uses.
Write each store statement in Statements and each payment that reached your bank in Payments Received. The gap, the days overdue and the fee check fill in by themselves.
Write each payment to a freelancer or provider in Job Payments. Known Payments Due lists the open ones in the order to pay them, with the cash left after each.
Write every expense in Expenses with its category, its vendor and whether the receipt is on file. Expenses by Category and Month compares each month with your own budget in Cost Categories.

Write the totals of each month in Profit and Loss by Month and Cash by Month, and the tax you set aside and paid in Tax Set-aside by Month. Revenue, costs, profit, closing cash and the pot balance fill in.

Read Cash Forecast for the next 12 months. Choose Base, Best or Worst on Start; Worst is sales minus 20 percent. The tools show the first low-cash month and the largest owner draw that holds your floor.

Type the five figures that come from your other parts in Health Check Areas (ad return, store dependence, two read-through figures and titles under break-even). The verdicts and the three actions fill in.
For a small press keep one row per pen name in Authors and Shares and one statement per pen name and month in Author Statements; a first author sets the share to 100 percent.

Use the 18 calculators for the weekly cash decisions, print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and tap a message link to send a text with the details already written in. Figures are estimates until the stores pay.

listing.title: Author and Self-Publisher Cash Flow Forecast, Tax Set-aside and Expense Tracker Excel Template: Owner Draw, Health Check, Author Statements
listing.headline: Know if you can pay what you owe, set tax aside and see what is left for you
listing.description:
Run the money side of an author or small publishing business in one Excel workbook. Built for an independent author who publishes under one or two pen names, often with a part-time assistant and freelancers paid per job. Cash Forecast looks 12 months ahead from your own history: expected royalties by pay month (each store's delay is a number you edit), known contractor payments, ad budget, expenses, tax set-aside and owner draw, with Base, Best and Worst scenarios (Worst is sales minus 20 percent) and a low-cash flag against your own floor.

Known Payments Due lists open payments to freelancers in the order to pay them, with the cash left after each. Cash for the Next 30 Days says pay now, pay in parts or hold the draw. Owner Draw Planner finds the largest steady draw that keeps your floor. Tax Set-aside by Month keeps the pot, the payments and the shortfall against your next payment (the percent is yours: confirm it with your tax adviser). Expenses by Category and Month compare each month with your own budget, and Year-end Summary Lines gather the pack for your adviser.

Health Check Areas scores twelve areas green, amber or red against your own targets and turns the worst three into actions. A small press gets Author Statements per pen name with shares, advance recouped, costs charged back and the amount payable, plus a shares check and an advance tracker.

18 calculators, 12 printable sheets, 12 documents, 12 checklists and 34 ready text messages to the accountant, the assistant, freelancers and the author are included. This is part eight of the Author and Self-Publisher Business suite. A standard .xlsx workbook with no macros and no subscription, with a demo copy full of sample data to explore first. Figures are estimates until the stores pay, every target is your own number, and it helps you keep track without promising any income.
